documents.title: Academic Integrity (Policy 6Hx28:8-11)
documents.summary: A general academic-integrity policy that mentions AI once, in its list of cheating examples. Work generated by AI counts as cheating unless the use has been explicitly permitted; the rest of the policy sets faculty and student duties and the sanction process without AI-specific content.
documents.stance_why: The only AI language lists submitting an assignment 'generated by Artificial Intelligence (AI), unless the use of AI has been explicitly permitted' as cheating, so AI-generated work is banned unless permitted, which is restrict. Whether it is permitted is left to faculty, but the document itself states the ban-by-default.

units.why: The passage says AI-generated submissions are cheating 'unless the use of AI has been explicitly permitted', so it sets the rule that applies when no permission is given. Actor is student, phase general, modality must-not, type P06 (fallback when silent) rather than P19 because the exception clause defines the default.
units.anchor: generated by Artificial Intelligence (AI), unless the use of AI has been explicitly permitted.
units.policy: Submitting an assignment generated by AI is cheating unless the use of AI has been explicitly permitted.
units.fit_note: The text does not mention syllabus silence; it sets AI-generated work as prohibited unless explicitly permitted, which also overlaps P19.

units.why: The sentence lists AI-generated submissions among 'Examples of cheating', so unauthorized AI use is classified as academic dishonesty handled by integrity processes. Actor is student, phase when-misuse, type P36 because it classifies the act as cheating rather than stating a penalty.
